la:verb:exspecto.html:
ex-specto (expect-), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to look out for a thing (syn.: prospecto, opperior, maneo, moror, praestolor).
Objectively, to await, expect something that is to come or to take place, to be waiting for, etc. (very freq. and class.). —Constr. with the acc., with rel.-clauses, with dum, si, ut, quin, or absol.; very rarely with object-clause.
In gen.
With acc.: caritatem,: alicujus mortem,: cum ea Scipio dixisset silentioque omnium reliqua ejus exspectaretur oratio,: injurias,: transitum tempestatis,: adventum alicujus,; : eventum pugnae,fin.: scilicet ultima semper Exspectanda dies homini est,: cenantes haud animo aequo Exspectans comites,i. e. waiting till they have done eating, et saep.; cf.: exspectandus erit annus,I must wait a year,. —
With relative and esp. interrogative clauses: exspectabat populus atque ora tenebat rebus, utri magni victoria sit data regni, Enn. ap. (Ann. s. 90, ed. Vahl.): exspecto, quo pacto, etc.,: exspecto, quid ad ista,; : quid hostes consilii caperent, exspectabat,: exspectante Antonio, quidnam esset actura,: ne utile quidem, quam mox judicium fiat, exspectare,; so, quid exspectas quam mox ego dicam, etc.,: et, quam mox signis collatis dimicandum sit, in dies exspectet,; : exspectans, quando, etc.,.—
With dum, si, ut, etc.: ne exspectetis meas pugnas dum praedicem,: ne exspectemus quidem, dum rogemur,: exspectas fortasse, dum dicat, etc.,: exspectare, dum hostium copiae augerentur,: nec dum repetatur, exspectat,: Caesar non exspectandum sibi statuit, dum, etc.,; cf.: nec vero hoc loco exspectandum est, dum, etc.,: rusticus exspectat, dum defluat amnis,: jam dudum exspecto, si tuum officium scias,: exspecto si quid dicas,: hanc (paludem) si nostri transirent, hostes exspectabant,; : nisi exspectare vis ut eam sine dote frater conlocet,: mea lenitas hoc exspectavit, ut id quod latebat, erumperet,: nisi forte exspectatis ut illa diluam, quae, etc.,: neque exspectant, ut de eorum imperio ad populum feratur,: quare nemo exspectet, ut, etc.,; ; ; —Pass. impers.: nec ultra exspectato, quam dum Claudius Ostiam proficisceretur,: cum omnium voces audirentur, exspectari diutius non oportere, quin ad castra iretur,—
Absol.: comites ad portam exspectare dicunt,: diem ex die exspectabam, ut statuerem, quid esset faciendum,: exspectent paullum et agi ordine sinant,.—
With object-clause: cum expectaret effusos omnibus portis Aetolos in fidem suam venturos, Weissenb. ad loc.: venturum istum,.—*
Transf., of an abstract subject, like maneo, to await: seu me tranquilla senectus Exspectat seu, etc.,.
To look for with hope, fear, desire, expectation, to hope for, long for, expect, desire; to fear, dread, anticipate, apprehend.
With acc.: reliquum est, ut tuam profectionem amore prosequar, reditum spe exspectem,; cf.: quod magna cum spe exspectamus, E. fin.: ego jam aut rem aut ne spem quidem exspecto,fin.: magnum inceptas, si id exspectas, quod nusquam'st, : quam (rem) avidissime civitas exspectat,: longiores (epistolas) exspectabo vel potius exigam,: finem laborum omnium,: illum ut vivat, optant, meam autem mortem exspectant scilicet,to wish,: fama mortis meae non accepta solum sed etiam exspectata est,; cf. in the pun with I.: cum Proculeius quereretur de filio, quod is mortem suam exspectaret, et ille dixisset, se vero non exspectare: Immo, inquit, rogo exspectes, Spald.: nescio quod magnum hoc nuntio exspecto malum,dread,: mortem,: multis de causis Caesar majorem Galliae motum exspectans,: 7, 43 fin.—With a personal object: pater exspectat aut me aut aliquem nuntium,: ite intro, filii vos exspectant intus,: hic ego mendacem usque puellam Ad mediam noctem exspecto,; cf. : video jam, illum, quem exspectabam, virum, cui praeficias officio et muneri,.—
Aliquid ab (rarely ex) aliquo (a favorite expression of Cicero): a te hoc civitas vel omnes potius gentes non exspectant solum, sed etiam postulant,; cf. : dixi Servilio, ut omnia a me majora exspectaret,: alimenta a nobis,: ab aliquo gloriam,fin.: tristem censuram ab laeso,: ut ex iis (proletariis) quasi proles civitatis exspectari videretur,.—
Aliquid ab or ex aliqua re (rare): aliquid ab liberalitate alicujus,: dedecus a philosopho,: omnia ex sua amicitia,.—
Aliquid aliquem (very rare): ne quid exspectes amicos, quod tute agere possies, Enn. ap. ; Sat. v. 38 Vahl.—
With object-clause: quid mihi hic adfers, quam ob rem exspectem aut sperem porro non fore?: exspecto cupioque te ita illud defendere,.—With inf. alone (cf. cupio), , ed. Rom.—
Absol. (very rare): cum mihi nihil improviso, nec gravius quam exspectavissem pro tantis meis factis evenisset,: aliquando ad verum, ubi minime exspectavimus, pervenimus,.—
Poet. transf., of an abstr. subject, to have need of, require: silvarumque aliae pressos propaginis arcus Exspectant,: neque illae (oleae) procurvam exspectant falcem rastrosque tenaces,; cf.: lenta remedia et segnes medicos non exspectant tempora mea,.—Hence, exspectātus (expect-), a, um, P. a. (acc. to II.), anxiously expected, longed for, desired, welcome (class.): carus omnibus exspectatusque venies,; cf.: venies exspectatus omnibus,; : quibus Hector ab oris exspectate venis?: sensi ego in exspectatis ad amplissimam dignitatem fratribus tuis,who were expected to arrive at the highest dignities of the state,: ubi te exspectatum ejecisset foras,i. e. whose death is waited, longed for, Ruhnk.—Comp.: nimis ille potuit exspectatior venire,.—Sup.: adventus suavissimus exspectatissimusque, a: litterae,: triumphus,—
In the neutr. absol.: quis non diversa praesentibus contrariaque exspectatis aut speret aut timeat?: hosti Ante exspectatum positis stat in agmine castris,before it was expected,; so, ante exspectatum,; ; : ille ad patrem patriae exspectato revolavit maturius,than was expected,.

la:noun:exspectatio.html:
exspectātĭo (expect-), ōnis, f.
id.
,
an awaiting, expecting, expectation (very freq. and class.; in sing. and plur.).
With gen. obj.: si spes est exspectatio boni, mali exspectationem esse necesse est metum,: harum rerum,: acerbior reliquorum,; cf. poenarum,: tanta vel animi vel ingenii tui, ut, etc.,; cf.: sustines non parvam exspectationem imitandae industriae nostrae,: majorem exspectationem mei faciam quam, etc.,; cf.: Varronis sermo facit exspectationem Caesaris,: quotidiana rerum novarum,: maximi belli,: rerum,: ejus rei,: desiderii,: nostri consilii,: audiendi, et saep. —In plur.: crebras exspectationes nobis tui commoves,.—
With de: quantam tu mihi moves exspectationem de sermone Bibuli!: plenus sum exspectatione de Pompeio,.—
With a rel.-clause: eo me major exspectatio tenet, quibusnam rationibus ea tanta vis comparetur,. —In plur.: nunc has exspectationes habemus duas: unam, etc., alteram, etc.,.—
Absol.: ne sis in exspectatione,: pendeo animi exspectatione Corfiniensi, in qua de salute rei publicae decernitur,: nolo plebem Romanam obscura spe et caeca exspectatione pendere,; cf.: omnia spe et exspectatione laudata,: aliquem in summam exspectationem adducere,: permagnam exspectationem imponere orationi,: M'. Curii causa nuper qua exspectatione defensa est?: praeter exspectationem,unexpectedly,: supra exspectationem,: exspectatione minor,: contra exspectationem omnium,.—In plur.: exspectationibus decipiendis,. —
The object of expectation or longing: gentium,: Israel,: pistorum laetitia,.

la:verb:exsequor.gloss: to follow after thoroughly, steadfastly accompany, go after, seek after, pursue persistently
senses: to follow after thoroughly, steadfastly accompany, go after, seek after, pursue persistently
to follow or accompany to the grave
to pursue (a course of action), follow up, carry out, enforce, perform, execute, accomplish, fulfill
to go through with in speaking, rehearse, relate, describe, say, tell
to pursue with vengeance or punishment, punish, avenge
la:verb:exsequor.html:
ex-sĕquor or exĕquor, cūtus, 3,
v. dep. a., to follow to the end, to pursue, follow.
In partic., to follow or accompany to the grave (cf. the deriv. exsequiae): funus, Massur. Sabin. ap. : aliquem omni laude et laetitia, Cic. poëta in Tusc. 1, 48, 115 (a transl. of ἐκπέμπειν, in Eurip.).
Trop. (class.; most freq. in the special significations).
In gen., to follow, follow after, accompany; to go after, to pursue: quae exanimata exsequitur aspectum tuum,: quid petam praesidi aut exsequar? Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 112 ed. Vahl.): non igitur dubium, quin aeternitatem maluerit exsequi, etc.,to follow after, take pattern after,: cur non omnes fatum illius (Pompei) una exsecuti sumus?followed, pursued, subjected ourselves to,; cf. : sectam meam exsecutae comites,joined,: suam quisque spem, sua consilia, communibus deploratis, exsequentes,: aerumnam, qs. to pursue, i. e. to undergo, suffer, endure, : egestatem,: mortem,: probrum,.—
In partic.
To follow up, prosecute, carry out; to perform, execute, accomplish, fulfil (syn.: conficio, perficio, perago, consummo, patro, perpetro, absolvo): nullam rem oportet dolose aggrediri, nisi Astute accurateque exsequare,; cf.: est difficile id non exsequi usque ad extremum,: inceptum hoc itiner perficere exsequar, and 88: incepta,: imperium,: mandata vestra,: omnia regis officia et munera,; cf.: munus officii (with tueri),: munus (with fungi),: negotia,: obsidiones,: scelus,: sermonem cum aliquo,to converse,: cum civitas armis jus suum exsequi conaretur, to assert, maintain, * : comptam et mitem orationem,.—With a rel.-clause: quem locum ipse capturus esset, cogitando aut quaerendo exsequebatur,: summa omnia cum cura inquirendo exequebatur,. 3, 2.—With ut: mihi Exsequi certa res est, ut abeam Potius hinc ad forum, quam domi cubem,.—
To go through with in speaking, to relate, describe, say, tell (freq. since the Aug. period): quae vix verbis exsequi possum,: quidam exsecuti sunt verbosius,: si omnia exsequi velim, : haec omnia copiosius,: quae diligentius,: quae divine in Oratore (Tullius),: caelestia dona aërii mellis,; cf.: laudes brassicae,: numerum subtiliter,: sententias,: vetera facunde,: vera,: imagines et elogia universi generis, et saep.—
To pursue with punishment, to punish, avenge (perh. not ante-Aug.): omnia scire, non omnia exsequi,: deorum hominumque violata jura,: injurias accusationibus,: delicta,: doloris exsequendi jus,: justum dolorem,.—Absol.: pater caedetur? defendam: caesus est? exsequar, Sen. de Ira, 1, 12; .—Once with a pers. object: me L. Tarquinium Superbum cum scelerata coniuge, etc., ferro, igni exsecuturum,to pursue, (MSS.; Weissenb. et al. exacturum).—Hence, exsĕ-quens (exeq-), entis, P. a. (acc. to II.), searching after, studious of: memoriarum veterum exsequentissimus,.!*? exsequi as pass.: quaerebatur an prioris judicis sententia exsequi possit, could be carried out (cf. II. B. supra), .—Hence, exsĕcūtus (exec-), a, um, in pass. signif.: exsecuto regis imperio,executed,.

la:verb:exstinguo.html:
ex-stinguo (ext-), nxi, nctum, 3 (archaic
perf. subj. exstinxit, for exstinxerit, .—Contracted forms exstinxsti, ; Pac. ap. ; and exstinxem,), v. a., to put out what is burning, to quench, extinguish (class.; esp. freq. in Cic. and in the trop. signif.).
Lit.: recens exstinctum lumen,: exstincta lumina,: faces,: lucernam,; cf.: senes mori sic videntur ut sua sponte nulla adhibita vi consumptus ignis exstinguitur,goes out,: ignem,: incendium,: sol exstinguitur,: exstincto calore ipsi exstinguimur, id. N. D. 2, 9, 23: calx exstincta,i. e. slaked,.—
Transf., to deprive of life or strength, to kill, destroy: animam alicui,: nolite, hunc jam natura ipsa occidentem velle maturius exstingui vulnere vestro,; cf. : juvenem fortuna morbo exstinxit,: vir egregius exstinctus,cut off,; ; ; ; ; et saep.: rapitur miser exstinguendus Messalinae oculis,: vel modico tepore sucus exstinguitur,i. e. is dried up,: mammas,: odorem alii,to destroy,: venena,to render powerless,: aquam Albanam dissipatam rivis, to consume, get rid of, an old prophecy in .—
Trop., to abolish, destroy, annihilate, annul (syn.: tollo, deleo, opprimo, diruo, everto, demolior, destruo; opp. inflammo): tyrannis institutis leges omnes exstinguuntur atque tolluntur,: ea, quae antea scripserat,: improbitas exstinguenda atque delenda est,: potentiam exstinguere atque opprimere,; but also distinguished from opprimere: ut exstinctae potius amicitiae quam oppressae esse videantur,extinct,: ad sensus animorum atque motus vel inflammandos vel etiam exstinguendos,: sermo omnis ille oblivione posteritatis extinguitur,; cf.: exstinctis rumoribus,: ad ejus salutem exstinguendam,: nomen populi Romani,: superiorem gloriam rei militaris,: memoriam publicam,: gratiam,: familiaritates,: invidiam,: infamiam,: causam nascentem dissensionis, Matius in : consuetudinem,: reliquias belli,: bellum civile,: jus pignoris,; cf. fideicommissum,: actionem,

senses: to stand out (as), to stand out in regard to (+ dative)
to be manifest, to be apparent or appear
la:verb:exsisto.html:
ex-sisto or existo, stĭti, stĭtum, 3, v. n. (
act. ), to step out or forth, to come forth, emerge, appear (very freq. and class.).
Prop.
In gen.: e latebris,: ab inferis,; : anguem ab ara exstitisse,; cf.: vocem ab aede Junonis ex arce exstitisse (shortly before: voces ex occulto missae; and: exaudita vox est a luco Vestae),: est bos cervi figura, cujus a media fronte inter aures unum cornu exsistit excelsius,: submersus equus voraginibus non exstitit,; cf. : nympha gurgite medio,: hoc vero occultum, intestinum ac domesticum malum, non modo non exsistit, verum, etc.,does not come to light,.—
In partic., with the accessory notion of originating, to spring, proceed, arise, become: vermes de stercore,: quae a bruma sata sunt, quadragesimo die vix exsistunt,: ut si qui dentes et pubertatem natura dicat exsistere, ipsum autem hominem, cui ea exsistant, non constare natura, non intelligat, etc.,: ex hac nimia licentia ait ille, ut ex stirpe quadam, exsistere et quasi nasci tyrannum,; ; cf.: ex luxuria exsistat avaritia necesse est,; ut exsistat ex rege dominus, ex optimatibus factio, ex populo turba et confusio,: ut plerumque in calamitate ex amicis inimici exsistunt,; for which: videtisne igitur, ut de rege dominus exstiterit? etc.,: ex quo exsistit id civitatis genus,: hujus ex uberrimis sermonibus exstiterunt doctissimi viri,; cf. : ex qua (disserendi ratione) summa utilitas exsistit,: sermo admirantium, unde hoc philosophandi nobis subito studium exstitisset,: exsistit hoc loco quaestio subdifficilis,: magna inter eos exsistit controversia,: poëtam bonum neminem sine inflammatione animorum exsistere posse,: exsistit illud, ut, etc., it ensues, follows, that, etc., ; cf.: ex quo exsistet, ut de nihilo quippiam fiat,.
Transf., to be visible or manifest in any manner, to exist, to be: ut in corporibus magnae dissimilitudines sunt, sic in animis exsistunt majores etiam varietates,: idque in maximis ingeniis exstitit maxime et apparet facillime,: si exstitisset in rege fides,: cujus magnae exstiterunt res bellicae,: illa pars animi, in qua irarum exsistit ardor,: si quando aliquod officium exstitit amici in periculis adeundis, et saep.: neque ullum ingenium tantum exstitisse dicebat, ut, etc.,; cf.: talem vero exsistere eloquentiam, qualis fuit in Crasso, etc.,; nisi Ilias illa exstitisset,: cujus ego dignitatis ab adolescentia fautor, in praetura autem et in consulatu adjutor etiam exstitissem,; cf.: his de causis ego huic causae patronus exstiti,: timeo, ne in eum exsistam crudelior,: sic insulsi exstiterunt, ut, etc.,.

la:verb:exsculpo.gloss: to dig out or carve out
senses: to dig out or carve out
la:verb:exsculpo.html:
ex-sculpo (exculp-), psi, ptum, 3, v. a.
To dig out, cut out, chisel out, carve.
Lit.: terram unde exsculpserant, fossam vocabant, Müll.: foramina arborum exsculpta digitos sex. : nescio quid e quercu exsculpseram, quod videretur simile simulacri,: signum ex molari lapide,; cf. .—
Transf., prov.: leoni esurienti ex ore exsculpere praedam, said of any thing exceedingly difficult or daring, Lucil. ap. . —
Trop., to get out, elicit, extort: ex aliquo verum,: in quaestione vix exsculpsi, ut diceret,obtained,.—*
To scratch out, erase: hos versus Lacedaemonii exsculpserunt,.

la:verb:exsulto.gloss: to spring vigorously, leap or jump up
senses: to spring vigorously, leap or jump up
la:verb:exsulto.html:
exsulto (exult-), āvi, ātum, 1,
v. freq. n. [id.], to spring vigorously, to leap or jump up (class.; esp. in the trop. signif.).
Lit.: equi ferocitate exsultantes,: equi,: exsultantes loligines,: pisciculi, id. Fragm. ap. : pecora exsultantia,: taurus in herba,; cf. : (curetes) in numerum exsultant,i. e. dance,.—
Of inanimate subjects: sanguis emicat exsultans alte,: pila exsultat,: exsultant aestu latices,; cf. : exsultant vada atque aestu miscentur harenae,: glaebae,: densiores circa pampini exsultant, spring up, i. e. come up, grow up, : breves (syllabae) si continuantur, exsultant,to skip, hop,.—
Trop.
In gen., to gambol about, move freely, expatiate: hic (in pectore) exsultat pavor ac metus,riot, gambol,: cum sit campus, in quo exsultare possit oratio,; cf.: in reliquis (orationibus) exsultavit audacius (Demosthenes),: assurgendi exsultandique in laudando licentia,: solidos novus exsultabis in actus,will undertake with alacrity,.—
In partic., to exult, rejoice exceedingly; to run riot, to revel; to vaunt, boast: exsultantem te et praefidentem tibi repriment legum habenae, Poët. ap. ; cf.: rex ille (Tarquinius) victoriis divitiisque subnixus, exsultabat insolentiā,; and: exsultasse populum insolentiā libertatis,: exsultare eam (partem animi) in somno immoderateque jactari,: exsultare voluptate, id. Fragm. ap. (Rep. 3, 36 ed. Mos.): laetitiā,; (with temere gestiens); ; : gaudio,: victoriā,; cf. successu,: gestis,: vana spe, et saep.: in ruinis alicujus,

: in omni crudelitate, id. Fragm. ap. (Rep. 2, 41 ed. Mos.): Graeci exsultant, quod, etc.,: dum histrio in cubiculum principis exsultaverit (= ἐξορχήσαιτο, Gronov.), (al. insultaverit).—Absol.: illa theatra (i. e. spectatores) exsultant, Mos. N. cr.: furorem exsultantem reprimere,; cf.: exsultantem laetitiam comprimere,: laus in qua maxime ceterorum exsultat oratio,.—Hence, ex-sultans (exult-), antis, P. a. *

(Acc. to I. B. fin.) Of short syllables, skipping, hopping: paululum morae damus inter ultimum ac proximum verbum ... alioqui sit exsultantissimum et trimetri finis,.—
(Acc. to II. B.)
Boastful, vain-glorious: turbati aut exsultantis animi motus,.—
Of an orator or an oration, diffuse, prolix: fiunt pro grandibus tumidi ... laetis corrupti, compositis exsultantes,; cf. ; ; (with remissae); 10, 4, 1: Cicero supra modum exsultans et superfluens,.— Hence, * Adv.: exsultanter, diffusely, at large; only comp.: quae hilarius et quasi exsultantius scripsi,.

la:noun:exsilium.html:
exsĭlĭum or exĭlĭum, ii, n.
exsul
,
banishment, exile.
Prop.: exsilium non supplicium est, sed perfugium portusque supplicii ... cum homines vincula, neces, ignominiasque vitant, quae sunt legibus constitutae, confugiunt quasi ad aram in exsilium,: exsilium triplex est; aut certorum locorum interdictio, aut lata fuga, ut omnium locorum interdicatur praeter certum locum, aut insulae vinculum, id est relegatio in insulam,: exsilio et relegatione civium ulciscentes tribunos,; so with relegatio,: exsilium iis (terribile est), quibus quasi circumscriptus est habitandi locus, etc.,: exacti in exsilium innocentes,: expulsus in exsilium,: pulsus in exsilium,: eicere aliquem in exsilium,: ire, proficisci in exsilium,; : mittere in exsilium,; ; ; ; : esse in exsilio,: de exsilio reducere,: revocare de exilio,: ab exsilio reducere,: ab exsilio revocare,; ; 2, 92; : jam redii de exsilio, et saep.—Prov.: exilium patitur patriae qui se denegat, (Rib.).—
Transf. (mostly poet. and post-Aug.).
A place of exile, a retreat: quodvis exsilium his est optatius quam patria,: Octavium et Antistium egressos exsilium, in easdem insulas redegit, : tutum orabant,: diversa quaerere,: multa patere fugienti,: exsilium patria sede mutare,.—*
(Abstr. pro concreto.) In plur.: exsilia, those who are banished, exiles: plenum exsiliis mare,.

la:verb:exspectandus.gloss: which is to be waited for
senses: which is to be waited for

la:verb:exsto.html:
ex-sto (ext-), āre, v. n. (
part. fut. exstaturus, ; Pand. 47, 2, 78 al.), to stand out or forth, to project, to stand above.
Prop.: (milites) cum capite solo ex aqua exstarent,; for which: super aequora celso collo,: aquis (navis),; cf. absol., : ferrum de pectore, 128: de arbore (surculus),: ossa sub incurvis lumbis,: aedificia modice ab humo exstantia,: paulum supra terram,.—Poet. with acc.: aliquem,to overtop,.—
Trop. (syn.: emineo, eniteo), to be prominent, stand forth, be conspicuous: quo magis id, quod erit illuminatum. exstare atque eminere videatur,: haec enitere et exstare aliquatenus,: arma tubaeque sonent, vox et tua noctibus exstet,predominate, be heard above,.—
Meton. (causa pro effectu), to be visible, show itself, appear;

to be extant

, to exist, to be (most freq., esp. of inanim. and abstr. subjects): hominum nemo exstat, qui, etc.,: auctor doctrinae ejus non exstat,. pecunia, cujus auctor non exstat, : Sarmenti domina exstat,still lives,: exstant hujus fortitudinis impressa vestigia,: exstant epistolae Philippi ad Alexandrum,: litterae,: leges,: orationes,: clarorum virorum non minus otii quam negotii rationem exstare oportere, Cato ap. : sine oculis non potest exstare officium et munus oculorum,; : video hoc in numero neminem, cujus non exstet in me suum meritum,: studium nostrum,.—
Impers., with a subject or rel.-clause (very rare): quem vero exstet et de quo sit memoriae proditum eloquentem fuisse, etc.,: apparet atque exstat, utrum simus earum (artium) rudes an didicerimus,—Hence, ex-stans, ntis, P. a., projecting, prominent; comp. partes exstantiores, .

senses: to renounce, abandon, relinquish, leave behind
la:verb:exsolvo.html:
ex-solvo, solvi, sŏlūtum, 3 (
per diaeresin exsolŭātur, : exsolŭïsse,; cf. solvo, init.), v. a., to loose, unloose, to unbind, untie, undo (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.
In gen.: nexus,: Am. Agedum, eam solve cistulam. So. Quid ego istam exsolvam? undo, unseal, : properans exsolvi restim,: catenas Caecinae,: vincula,; : pugionem a latere,to ungird,: venas praebere exsolvendas,to be opened,; ; : brachia ferro eodem ictu,: amictus,to pull off,: venenum exsoluta alvo transmisit,i. e. in a flux, diarrhœa,.—Of an inanimate subject: (ignis) exsolvit glaciem,dissolves, melts,.—
In partic.
To set loose, release, deliver, free (mostly poet.): aliquem vinclis,; so, exsolutus vinculis,: jube sis me exsolvi cito,: sese e nervis (animae),; cf. : se paulatim corpore (said of one dying),: quo (sanguine),.—
In mercant. lang. (qs. to free from obligation, v. solvo, to discharge, pay a debt): nomina mea, per deos, expedi, exsolve (for which, shortly after: hoc quod debeo plane expedias et solutum relinquas), : aes alienum,: pretium,: multiplicem sortem,: dotem uxori,: legata, et saep. —
Trop.
In gen., to throw off, lay aside, rid one's self of a thing: legis nexus,: metus,i. e. to lay aside,: pudorem,: robur peditum ad exsolvendum obsidium ducit,i. e. to raise,.—
In partic.
To release, free from any thing: animum artis nodis religionum,; : animos religione,: populum religione,: se occupationibus,: aliquem errore, suspicione,: aliquem aere alieno,: curis,: sollicitudine,: contumeliā,: poenā,: custode, et saep.—
To discharge, pay a debt or an obligation: de tertio genere se scripsit dicturum, nec exsolvit quod promiserat,but did not keep his promise,: vota (deo),; (opp. se obligare): jus jurandum,: fidem,to fulfil one's promise,: praemia, poenas alicui,to award,: gratiam recte factis, alicujus,; cf. grates,to render, give,: beneficia,to repay, requite,; cf.: vicem beneficio,: poenas morte,to suffer,; cf. —
To solve, explain any thing enigmatical or obscure: perfacile est parili ratione exsolvere nobis, quare, etc.,.

la:noun:exsul.gloss: A person who is exiled, exile, wanderer.
senses: A person who is exiled, exile, wanderer.
la:noun:exsul.html:
ex-sul or exul, ŭlis, comm.
usual. referred to solum; one who is banished from his native soil; but prob. from root sal-, Sanscr. sar, to go; Lat. salire, saltare; cf.: praesul, consul, subsul, Corss. Ausspr. 2, 71
,
a banished person, wanderer, exile.
Prop.: omnes scelerati atque impii, quos leges exsilio affici volunt, exsules sunt, etiamsi solum non mutarint,: civitas exsulem regem (Tarquinium) esse jussit,: exsules damnatique,; cf.: capitis damnati exsulesque,: cum Hannibal Carthagine expulsus Ephesum ad Antiochum venisset exsul,: cum vagus et exsul erraret atque undique exclusus,: exsules restituti,; : reducere,; : dives, inops, Romae, seu fors ita jusserit, exsul,.—With gen. (mostly poet.): patriae quis exsul se quoque fugit?.—With abl.: nunc vero exsul patriā, domo,.—Prov.: exsuli ubest nusquam domus est, sine sepulchro mortuus, Publ. Syr. 155 (Speng.).—
As fem.: exsul Hypermnestra,; : (Latona) exsul erat mundi,.—Poet.: exul adhuc jacet umbra ducit,. —
Transf. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): exsul mentisque domusque,deprived of reason,: erret per urbem pontis exsul et clivi,: ciconia avis exsul hiemis, i. e. that leaves us in winter, Publ. Syr. ap. (Com. Fragm. p. 304 Rib.).

la:verb:exsuscito.html:
ex-suscĭto (exusc-), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to rouse from sleep, to awaken (class.).
Lit.: exsuscitate vostram huc custodem mihi,: te gallorum cantus exsuscitat,.—
Transf., of fire, to kindle: flammas exsuscitat aurā,: ne parvus ignis ingens incendium exsuscitet,. —
Trop., to stir up, rouse up, excite: quae cura exsuscitat animos et majores ad rem gerendam facit,; so, animum omnibus dictis,; and: animum clamore,: naturalem memoriam hac notatione,; cf. .

la:verb:exsilio.gloss: to spring, bound, leap or start out, up or forth
senses: to spring, bound, leap or start out, up or forth
la:verb:exsilio.html:
ex-sĭlĭo or exĭlĭo, ĭlŭi (exilivit, Poet. ap. M.; v. Rib. Com. Fragm. p. 118; :
exsilii,; ; ), 4, v. n.
salio
, to spring out, spring or bound forth, to spring or leap up, to start up (freq. and class.): puer citus e cunis exilit,: properans de sella exsiluit,: domo levis exsilit,: stratis,: gremio,: ut continuo exiliatis,: impetu perturbatus exsiluisti,; cf.: exsilui gaudio, I leaped for joy, Q. Cic. ap. : protinus exsilui, et saep.: foras,: ad te exsilui,I sprang to you,: (anguis) exsilit in siccum,: in obvia arma,: exiluit partus de vulnere matris,.—
Of inanimate subjects: Cicero noster, a quo Romana eloquentia exsiluit,took its rise,: et magno imperatori cor exsiluit, with eager expectation, id. de Ira, 2, 3, 3: tum quoque lumen Exsilit,; cf. : plus ut parte foras emergant exsiliantque (aquae),: crinis,: exsiluere oculi,started out,: exsiluere loco silvae, et saep.

la:verb:exsulo.gloss: to live in exile, be banished
senses: to live in exile, be banished
la:verb:exsulo.html:
exsŭlo or exŭlo, also arch. exsŏlo, exŏlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
[exsul].
Neutr., to be an exile or banished person, tolive in exile (class.): qui Romam in exsili um venisset, cui Romae exsulare jus esset,: ut exsulares,: aptissimus ad exulandum locus,: in Volscos exsulatum abiit,: exsulans atque egens,: apud Prusiam exsulans,; et saep.: alii exolatum abierant,; .—
Transf.: perii, nam domo exulo nunc: metuo fratrem, Ne intus sit,: cum omnes meo discessu exsulasse rem publicam putent,: peculatus ex urbe et avaritia si exulant,: etiam cum manent corpore, animo tamen exsulant,: quousque in regno exsulabo,be a stranger in my own country,.—
Act., to banish, exile a person (late Lat.): tunc iterum exulatur,; Dict. Cretens. 4, 4 fin.
la:verb:exsulo.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:verb:exscindo.html:
ex-scindo (exc-), ĭdi, issum, 3, v. a. (lit., to tear out; hence, in gen.),
to extirpate, destroy (syn.: delere, evertere, vastare).
Lit. (class.): templum sanctitatis, etc. ... inflammari, exscindi, funestari,; cf. ; ; ; ; ; : Pergama Argolicis telis,: domos,: ferro sceleratam gentem,: hostem,.—
Trop., to tear away: fortine animam hanc exscindere dextra indignum est visum? . (In , read excidisti).

la:adj:exsanguis.gloss: Deprived of blood, without or lacking in blood; bloodless.
senses: Deprived of blood, without or lacking in blood; bloodless.
la:adj:exsanguis.html:
ex-sanguis (exang-), e, adj.,
deprived of blood, without blood, bloodless (class.).
Lit.: unde animantum copia tanta Exos et exsanguis,: jacens et concisus plurimis vulneribus, extremo spiritu exsanguis et confectus,; cf.: exsanguis et mortuus concidisti,: hostes enervati atque exsangues,: exsanguia corpora mortuorum,: umbrae,.—
Transf., pale, wan: genae, Poët. ap. : exsanguis metu,; cf.: diffugimus visu exsangues,: herbae,.—Act.: cuminum,making pale, (cf.: cuminum omne pallorem bibentibus gignit,): horror,.—
Trop., powerless, feeble, weak: aridum et exsangue orationis genus,; cf.: exsanguis et attritus,: vox nimis exilis et exsanguis,: exsangues crudescunt luctibus anni (senectutis),: imperium,.

la:verb:exsupero.html:
ex-sŭpĕro (exup-), āvi, ātum (
gen. plur. part. sync. exsuperantum, Müll.), 1, v. n. and a. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Neutr., to mount up, appear above (very rare).
Lit.: exsuperant flammae; furit aestus ad auras,.—
Trop., to get the upper hand, to overcome, prevail, excel: sol et vapor omnis,: arma capessant, Et si non poterunt exsuperare, cadant,: praesens dolor,: quantum ipse feroci Virtute exsuperas,: Hannibal exsuperans astu,.—
Act., to project or tower above any thing, to surmount, rise above, exceed.
Lit.: vites exsuperant ulmos,: exsuperat jugum,passes over,: clivum,: amnem,: Nilus exsuperavit sedecim cubita,; cf.: binas libras ponderis,.—
Trop.
To surpass, exceed: quis homo te exsuperavit usquam gentium impudentiā? Poët. ap. : omnes Tarquinios superbiā,: genus morum nobilitate,: aliquid latitudine,: laudes alicujus,: cuncta exsuperans patrimonia census,: tu vero, pater, vive et me quoque exsupera,survive, outlive,: aestatem,to outlast,.—
To be too much for, to overpower, overcome: id summum exsuperat Jovem, Poët. in : materia vires exsuperante meas,: caecum consilium,: multitudo Gallorum, sensum omnem talis damni exsuperans,.—Hence, exsŭpĕrans (exup-), antis, P. a. (acc. to I. B.), surpassing, excellent, supreme (post-class.): mulier exsuperanti forma,.—Comp.: uter esset exsuperantior, certabatur, .—Sup., .
la:verb:exsupero.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:verb:exstruo.gloss: to pile, heap or build up
senses: to pile, heap or build up
to build up, raise, rear, erect, construct
la:verb:exstruo.html:
ex-strŭo (extr-), xi, ctum, 3, v. a.,
to pile or heap up (class.; syn.: struo, aedifico, condo, fundo).
Lit.
In gen.: magnum acervum (librorum),; cf.: stramenta in acervum exstrui debent,to be heaped up,: mensae conquisitissimis epulis exstruebantur,heaped, bountifully furnished,: mensas,: caret exstructis mensis,; ; ; cf. canistros,to heap full,: focum lignis,: exstructis in altum divitiis,: divitias,.—
In partic. (acc. to struo, I. B. 1.), to build up, raise, rear, erect, construct: exstrui vetat (Plato) sepulcrum altius quam quod, etc.,: aedificium in alieno,: monumentum, molem opere magnifico,: theatrum,: tumulos,: aggerem in altitudinem pedum octoginta,; ; : turres,; ; : rogum,; : quas (divitias) profundant in exstruendo mari et montibus coaequandis,to build up, fill with buildings,: aream sibi sumpsit, in qua civitatem exstrueret arbitratu suo,.—
Trop.
In gen.: verba sint ad poëticum quendam numerum exstructa,put together, constructed,: poëma,: crimen unum vocibus multis,to exaggerate, magnify,.—
In partic. (acc. to I. B.): exstrue animo altitudinem excellentiamque virtutum,build up,; cf.: non modo fundata sed etiam exstructa disciplina,.—Hence, * ex-structus (extr-), a, um, P. a., highbuilt, lofty: exstructissimae species aedificiorum,.

la:verb:exsecror.html:
ex-sē^cror (execr-), ātus, 1,
v. dep. a. and n.
sacer
, to curse, execrate.
Prop. (class.; syn.: abominor, detestor, abhorreo, horreo, aversor, devoveo): te oderunt, tibi pestem exoptant, te exsecrantur,; (with male precari),: aliquem,; : consilia Catilinae,: severitatem nimiam et assidua belli pericula,: superbiam regis,: litem, et saep.: in se ac suum ipsius caput,: exsecratus deinde in caput regnumque Prusiae,: exsecratur Thyestes, ut naufragio pereat Atreus,: verba exsecrantia, et saep.—*
Transf., to take a solemn oath with imprecations (against its infringement): eamus omnis execrata civitas (= his votis cum exsecratione conceptis),; cf. v. 18.!*? *
Also, act.: exsecro, āre: exsecrabant se ac suos, Afran. ap. ; cf. P.—
exsē^crātus, a, um, in pass. signif. and as P. a., accursed, execrable, detestable: non te exsecratum populo Romano, non detestabilem, etc. ... scias,: exsules duo, Cato ap. P.: columna,; .—Sup.: exsecratissima auguria,.—
exsē^-crandus, a, um, as P. a., detestable (late Lat.); : libido, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 6, 4, 2 Huschke.—Sup.: exsecrandissimum nefas,.

la:verb:exserto.html:
exserto (exert-), āre, v. freq. a.
exsero
.
To stretch out, thrust forth: Scyllam Ora exsertantem,: linguam, Claud. Quadrig. ap. : lacertos,: aurem per aulaeum,i. e. listening eagerly,.—*
(Acc. to exsero, I. B.) To uncover, to bare: humeros,.

la:verb:exspiro.html:
ex-spīro (expīro), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic. and Caes.).
Act., to breathe out, to emit, to blow out, to exhale, give out: animam pulmonibus, Lucil. ap. : animam medios in ignes,: auras,: flumen sanguinis de pectore,; cf.: flammas pectore,: odorem de corpore,: sonos per saxa (unda),: colorem (uniones),.—
Poet. transf.: cadavera vermes,i. e. send forth, produce,: silva comas tollit fructumque exspirat in umbras,i. e. spreads out into foliage,.—
Exspirare animam, to expire, die, —
Neutr.
To rush forth, come forth, be exhaled.
Lit.: per fauces montis ut Aetnae Exspirent ignes,: ignis foras (with exire in auras),: vis fera ventorum,: halitus Averni,: unguenta,evaporate,: vis, Lucil. ap. .—*
Trop.: irae pectoris exspirantes,.—
To breathe one's last, to expire.
Lit.: ut per singulos artus exspiraret, Dietsch.: atram tundit humum exspirans,: ubi perire jussus exspiravero,: inter primam curationem exspiravit,: inter verbera et vincula,: extremus exspirantis hiatus,; ; ; ; ; ; ; .— Pass. impers.: quoniam membranā cerebri incisā statim exspiretur,: exspiravit aper dentibus apri,.—
Trop., to expire, perish, come to an end, cease: si ego morerer, mecum exspiratura res publica erat,: libertate jam exspirante,: ne res publica exspiraret,: criminis causa exspirat,becomes extinct, ceases,; : prior obligatio,.
la:verb:exspiro.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.

la:verb:exsequere.gloss: second-person singular present active imperative/indicative of exsequor
senses: second-person singular present active imperative/indicative of exsequor
having no share in, free from, deprived of
la:adj:exsors.html:
ex-sors (exors), sortis, adj.,
without lot, i. e. who has not cast a lot, who obtains a thing out of course; also, that for which a lot has not been cast, chosen, choice.
Prop. (poet.): te voluit rex magnus Olympi Talibus auspiciis exsortem ducere honorem,: ducunt exsortem (equum) Aeneae,; .—
Transf., in gen., having no share in, free from, deprived of.
With gen.: dulcis vitae,: amicitiae et foederis,: culpae,: periculi,: matrimoniorum,: cos exsors secandi,incapable of cutting,.—*
With dat.: hospes conflictui huic,

la:adj:exsaturabilis.html:
exsătŭrābĭlis, e, adj.
exsaturo
,
that may be satiated: pectus,.

la:adj:exsomnis.html:
ex-somnis (exomn-), e, adj.
somnus
,
sleepless, wakeful, watchful (poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf.: insomnis, vigil, vigilans): vir,: (Tisiphone) Vestibulum exsomnis servat noctesque diesque,; : animo exsomnis,

la:verb:exsurgo.html:
ex-surgo (exurgo), surrexi, 3, v. n. (archaic
inf. pres. pass. exsurgier, prol. fin.), to rise up, rise, to get up, stand up (class.).
Lit.: a genibus,: ex insidiis,: in plantas,: de nocte multa,: ubi erit accubitum semel, Ne quoquam exsurgatis, donec, etc.,: foras,: cum exsurgeret, simul arridens, etc.,: tu autem, nisi molestum est, paulisper exsurge,; cf.: exsurge quaeso,: acies ita instructa, ut pars in colles exsurgeret,: altior (to strike the more forcibly), et saep.—
Transf., of things as subjects: ubi Taurus ab Indico mari exsurgit,; cf. : inde alii ramuli exsurgunt,: cum jam vertigine tectum ambulat, et geminis exsurgat mensa lucernis, i. e. in the dizzy brain,.—
Trop., to rise up, rise, recover strength: ne quando recreata exsurgere atque erigere se possent, funditus sustulerunt,: (causa) numquam exsurgeret,: auctoritate vestra res publica exsurget,: grandis oratio naturali pulchritudine exsurgit,; dolor,.

la:noun:exsequiae.html:
exsĕquĭae (exequ-), ārum, f.
exsequor, I. B.
.
A funeral procession, funeral obsequies (freq. and class.; syn.: funus, pompa, justa, inferiae, feralia): funus, quo amici convenerant ad exsequias cohonestandas,; cf.: exsequias funeris prosequi,; and: funus innumeris exsequiis celebratum,: Clodii cadaver spoliatum imaginibus, exsequiis,: justis exsequiarum, id. Leg, 2, 17, 42: fertur in exsequiis matrona,: exsequiis rite solutis, et saep.: exsequias ire,to go to the funeral,; ; ; —
Transf., in late Lat., for reliquiae, the earthly remains, relics: humiliter sepultae Neronis,; ; Sext. .

la:verb:exseco.html:
ex-sĕco (also exĕco and exĭco, ), cŭi, ctum, 1 (
perf. subj. exsecaveris, ), v. a., to cut out or away.
Lit. (class.).
In gen.: vitiosas partes,: pestem aliquam tamquam strumam civitatis,: linguam,: cornu (frontis),: varices,: fetum ventri,: ventrem,: filium alicui mortuae,: nervos,: fundum armarii,.—
In partic., to cut, castrate, geld: vetus haec opinio Graeciam opplevit exsectum Caelum a filio Saturno,; ; ; and in a Greek construction: infelix ferro mollita juventus Atque exsecta virum,.—
Trop.: exsectus et exemptus honoribus senatoriis,.—Poet., of interest: quinas hic capiti mercedes exsecat (=extorquet, extundit),cuts out, deducts,.

la:noun:exsultatio.html:
exsultātĭo (exult-), ōnis, f.
id.
,
a springing up, leaping, frisking (post-Aug.).
Lit.: puerilis nimia exsultatio,; ; . —
Trop., excessive rejoicing, exultation: gaudium enim exsultatio, exsultationem tumor et nimia aestimatio sui sequitur, Sen. de Ira, 2, 21; cf.: laetitia dicitur exsultatio quaedam animi gaudio efferventior,; ;

la:verb:exsero.gloss: to stretch or thrust forth or out
senses: to stretch or thrust forth or out
la:verb:exsero.html:
ex-sero or exĕro, rŭi, rtum, 3,
v. a.; to stretch out or forth, to thrust out, put forth, to take out (mostly post-Aug.).
Lit.: Gallus linguam ab irrisu exserens,: linguam per os,: manum subter togam ad mentum,: brachia aquis,: caput ponto,; for which: caput ab Oceano,; cf.: herba Exserit e tepida molle cacumen humo,: enses,: creverat infans Quaerebatque viam, qua se exsereret,might come forth,: se domicilio (cochleae),: radicem ejus exserito,take out, tear up,: vincula,i. e. to throw off,.—
In partic., of parts of the body, exsertus, a, um, protruding from the dress, bare, uncovered: dextris humeris exsertis, bared, * ; cf. ; ; cf. transf. of the person: exsertus humero,; and in Greek construction: exserti ingentes humeros,: unum exserta latus Camilla,: truces exserta manus,; also absol.: exsertique manus vesana Cethegi,tucked up, prepared for the fight,: Latona,.—
Trop.
In gen.: exseram in librum tuum jus, quod dedisti,will avail myself of, make use of,: secreta mentis ore exserit,discloses,.—
In partic., to reveal, show, with an object-clause, : paulatim principem exseruit,i. e. showed himself as,. —Hence, exsertus (exert-), a, um, P. a.
Thrust forth, projecting: dentes apro, elephanto, etc.,.—
Open, evident, conspicuous: exserto bello,: cachinnus,i. e. unrestrained, loud,: exsertior opera,. —Adv.: exserte (acc. to B.), openly, clearly, loudly: clamitans,: jubet,.—Comp.: consurgere,.—Sup.: egit tribunatum (with severissime),very strictly, rigorously,.

la:noun:exstinctor.html:
ex-stinctor (ext-), ōris, m.
id.
,
an extinguisher (rare but class.).
Lit.: non exstinctor sed auctor incendii,.—
Transf., an annihilator, destroyer: ne exstinctor patriae, ne proditor, ne hostis appelletur,: regiae domus (Cassander),.—
Trop.: conjurationis, suppressor (opp. auctor et dux), Auct. Or. pro Domo, 38, 101: belli, Auct. Or. de Harusp. Resp. 23, 94.

la:verb:exstirpo.html:
ex-stirpo (ext-), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to pluck up by the stem or root, to root out, extirpate.
Lit. (only post-Aug.): arbores,; cf. lucos,; and: silva exstirpata procellis,: pilos de corpore toto,.— Transf.: silvestris ager decrescente luna utilissime exstirpatur,is cleared from stubble,: agros arboribus atque virgultis,.—
Trop., to root out, eradicate, extirpate (class.): vitia et funditus tollere,: ex animo humanitatem,: perturbationes,: nomina inimica libertati, Sen. de Ira, 1, 16 med.: virtutem Israël,.

la:adj:exsecrabilis.html:
exsē^crābĭlis (execr-), e, adj.
exsecror
.
Pass., execrable, accursed, detestable: exsecr. ac dirum solum,: nihil exsecrabilius,; —
Act., execrating: praeeuntibus exsecrabile carmen sacerdotibus,the song of cursing, of execration,: odium,i. e. raging, fearful,.—Adv.: exsē^crābĭlĭter, execrably (only in comp.): tanto exsecrabilius me oderam,.

la:verb:exspolio.html:
ex-spŏlĭo (expŏl-), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. (dep. form exspoliantur, Poët. ap. Don. 1769 P.: exspoliabantur, Quadrig. ap. ),
to spoil, pillage, plunder (class.).
Lit.: agrum Campanum, Quadrig. l. l.: ad expoliandum corpus, qui vulneraverat alacer gaudio accurrit,.—
Trop.: exercitu et provincia Pompeium,; cf.: hos vestro auxilio,: virtutem rerum selectione,: omnem honorem et dignitatem Caesaris,to deprive, dub. (al. spoliare): improbis sese artibus,.

la:verb:exspuo.html:
ex-spŭo (expuo), ŭi, ūtum, 3, v. n. and a.
, to spit out, to spit (not in Cic.).
Neutr.: cum ille gustasset et exspuisset,; : in mare, .—
Act.
Lit.: vina,: sanguinem,; : linguam in tyranni os,.—
Transf., to cast out, eject, expel, emit: quod mare (te) conceptum spumantibus exspuit undis?: argentum vivum optime purgat aurum, ceteras ejus sordes exspuens crebro jactatu,: rorem,: carbonem,: in litus purgamenta,: lacrumam,.—
Trop., to expel, banish, remove: miseriam ex animo,: rationem ex animo,.
la:verb:exspuo.inflection: ŭi, ūtum, 3, v. n. and a.

la:verb:exsicco.html:
ex-sicco (exicc-), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to dry up, make quite dry (class.).
In gen.: arbores,: sulcos,.—Transf., of an abstr. subject: ebrietas, donec exsiccetur,is exhaled, passes off,— Trop.: spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa,.—
In partic., to drain dry, to empty a bottle (= epotare, cum aliqua aviditatis significatione): lagenae furtim exsiccatae, Q. Cic. ap. ; for which poet.: vina culullis,; cf. of the sea: mare,—Hence, * exsiccātus (exicc-), a, um, P. a., dried up, dry, jejune: orationis genus,.

la:noun:exsecratio.html:
exsē^crātĭo (execr-), ōnis, f.
id.
.
Execration, malediction, curse: Thyestea ista exsecratio est: ut tu naufragio expulsus, etc.,: exierunt malis omnibus atque exsecrationibus,; ; ; § 6; ; —
Transf.
A solemn oath with an imprecation (if broken): aliquem exsecratione devincire,: ubi fides? ubi exsecrationes? ubi dextrae complexusque?; ; ; ; ; al.—
An abomination, a thing to be execrated, .

la:verb:exsorbeo.gloss: to suck up, out or in, gulp down, drain; exhaust

la:verb:exscribo.gloss: to write out or off, copy
senses: to write out or off, copy
la:verb:exscribo.html:
ex-scrībo (excr-), psi, ptum (btum), 3, v. a.,
to write out, write off, copy.
Lit. (rare but class.): tabulas in foro summa hominum frequentia exscribo; adhibentur in exscribendo ex conventu viri primarii,: complura exscripta de Magonis libris,: ex Plauti comoedia duos versus exscripsimus,.—
Transf. *
Of paintings, to copy: imagines exscribere et pingere,.—
In gen., to write or note down: nomina exscripta,: bonos in aliis tabulis exscriptos habet,.—*
Trop., to copy or take after, to resemble: filia totum patrem mira similitudine exscripserat,.
